summary: Pass. Every blocking finding from round 2 is closed by evidence in the checkout, and no new blocking issue was found. IMPL-R2-01 is closed: audit-tests.log now records 7 of 7 tests OK, including the empty-BD, real-fd snapshot, wrong-fd and Slurm-mask intersection regressions. The trailing MUNGE line is a site diagnostic printed after OK. IMPL-R2-02 is closed: evidence/pilot04 contains complete.json, status.json, schedule, gpu-inventory, affinity probes, gpu-tests (exitcode 0, 31 call passes, '31 passed'), input-validation (pass, 160.999 s, 8 workers, /proc read_bytes delta 46,846,976,000), all 14 case receipts with their commands and logs, sacct records and audit.json (state pass). In the sacct records, the parent, batch and extern records and all 18 numeric steps are COMPLETED 0:0, on lcls_g/gpu_premium, elapsed 00:15:27. IMPL-R2-03 is closed: bundle.json and complete.json give bundle commit e7c61f05a. bundle-comparison.json lists all 18 harness files with bundle hash equal to review-source hash. Because audit.py:46 requires complete['bundle']['commit'] to equal the commit passed in, the passing audit implies it was run with e7c61f05a. IMPL-R2-04 is closed: README, RESULTS and status.json describe the final state, all four jobs, the accepted job, the deferrals and node time (908+277+930+927 = 3042 s = 50m42s, leaving 18,558 s of the 6 h cap). IMPL-R1-01 is closed: the parallel validator keeps the full per-file checks, and the /proc read_bytes delta (about 46.8 GB, compared with about 2 TB for streaming every file) supports sparse header reads. It is correctly labelled as process/kernel counters, not Lustre wire traffic. IMPL-R1-04 (peak device memory) and IMPL-R1-06 (sizing/screen launcher) stay deferred and non-blocking, as accepted in round 2, and are disclosed as required before any full screen. The code changes are sound. fd_snapshot uses readlink and ignores fds that vanish. select_affinity intersects all 9 probe masks, checks that topology agrees, removes SMT siblings and needs at least 56 cores. The runner's affinity() requires the exact list to sit inside each step mask. audit.py recomputes the set from the probes and requires every rank of every case to match it. The reported rates in RESULTS.md agree with audit.json. Witness coverage in tail-b4-s2 adds up to 96,288 (19200+28800+28800+19488 = 1003×96). Both depth-2 four-BD receipts show every BD using two distinct streams. The three rejected attempts and their failure points are disclosed, and they contribute no accepted rates. The sweep is described as prepared only, not as a stripe ranking.

audit-tests.log: 7 tests listed, 'Ran 7 tests', OK. These match the 7 test methods in test_audit.py, including test_empty_bds_keep_global_partition, test_snapshot_excludes_closed_directory_handle, test_common_affinity_across_slurm_shapes and test_real_wrong_fd.

instrument.py:8-13: fd_snapshot uses os.readlink inside try/except OSError, so a /proc directory-listing fd that has vanished is skipped. The cached-handle identity check (lines 29-32) still fails closed.

support.py:54-62 select_affinity requires a single host, intersects all probe masks, requires topology to agree across probes, takes one CPU per (package, core) and requires at least 56. support.py:64-73 affinity() requires the 56 CPUs to be distinct, inside the step mask and with no SMT siblings, and reads the mask back after setting it.

audit.py:54-59 recomputes select_affinity from affinity.json probes, requires probe ranks [0,0,1,1,2,2,3,4,5] and requires every row of every case to equal that set. affinity.json lists 0-29 and 32-57 (56 CPUs) on nid003140, which matches the four-BD set described in pilot03/OUTCOME.md.

validate_data.py: 8 ThreadPoolExecutor workers run validate_one on each file. Each worker does the full SMD timeline, unbuffered pread(24) BD header checks, offset/size checks, the EOF check and count-2 witness reads. The merge rejects duplicate witness panels and requires all 32 panels.

limitations: No commands, tests or jobs were run. Every test result comes from committed evidence files.

Without git or hashing tools I could not recompute SHA-256 values. Byte equality of the harness files with bundle04 rests on evidence/pilot04/bundle-comparison.json and complete.json. That the latest commit adds only evidence and docs is accepted on that basis.
Raw witness.json and ranges.json reference arrays were excluded by scope. Their hash checks and the physical-range digest checks rest on the passing audit.json.

The audit recomputes the affinity selection from probes embedded in affinity.json. It does not re-read the raw affinity-*-r*.json files. I did not compare every raw probe file with affinity.json line by line.
I read only selected case receipts in detail (tail-b4-s2 and the stream fields of pilot-b4-s2). For the other cases I relied on the audit pass and summary values.
Backend/Lustre wire traffic, server-side cache state and peak device memory remain unmeasured, as the documentation discloses.
